meta.title: Sitcoms and related English-language comedies, around 1970 onward

scope.countries: Any; production country claims remain attributed where not independently checked.
scope.time_window: Original episodes aired in or after 1970; three retained premieres are from 1968 or 1969.
scope.coverage: Curated research catalog, not a complete census. Two inherited sketch-adjacent entries are explicitly classified and can be filtered out.
scope.well_regarded_policy: Keep curation membership separate from documented recognition. Candidates lacking adequate evidence are explicitly marked; presence in this file is not a certification of acclaim.

reconciliation.identity_policy: Preserve Claude canonical IDs for its 300 records, assign four new readable IDs, and retain every original key in id_aliases. Consumers must apply this mapping when importing older ratings; the current live tracker is not modified.
reconciliation.primary_tag_policy: Use one controlled primary vocabulary. Preserve ChatGPT annotations separately as legacy interpretations rather than automatically unioning inconsistent tags.
reconciliation.tag_weight_policy: Original order-based weights are preserved as unreviewed estimates and disabled by default. Their values are not measured intensity.

missing_value_policy.null: Unknown, not checked, or not applicable as described by field provenance.
missing_value_policy.empty_array: No entries recorded; not proof that the attribute or award is absent.
missing_value_policy.unknown_end_date: Does not imply a show is running. Consult the explicit status and its source.

statuses.documented_award_recognition: At least one series/animation award event cross-checked with the stated reference, or a primary award record. Includes nominations; does not establish universal esteem.
statuses.sourced_recognition_snapshot: Imported linked evidence for an award in any category, historical top-30 audience ranking, or RT critics snapshot of at least 80%. Evidence is dated and not newly re-audited.
statuses.audience_snapshot_threshold: Historical IMDb score at least 7.5/10 and at least approximately 5,000 votes in the supplied PDF. An editorial threshold, subject to sampling and source limitations.
statuses.needs_reputation_evidence: Candidate retained without sufficient documented evidence under these rules.

qualification_policy.default_recommendation_advice: Use views.documented_selection as the default eligible recommendation pool, and all_catalog_records for rating/history entry. Let users explicitly include candidates. Exclude watched shows independently of acclaim.

field_notes.years: Premiere/end years for the matched provider entity where available; not automatically a union of imported revival periods.
field_notes.status: Provider-reported running/ended/uncertain/upcoming/unknown, with a source. Not a renewal guarantee.
field_notes.seasons: Provider season records with an observed premiere date on or before built_on. Consult field_provenance for exceptions and numbering differences.
field_notes.reported_runs: Imported original/revival history. May combine distinct provider entities and is flagged for entity-boundary review; do not sum or treat as verified automatically.
field_notes.source_claims: Original imported date/status/season/run values retained for audit. They are not the preferred canonical values.
field_notes.awards: Explicit result and year convention. recorded_award_wins counts only stored entries, not lifetime totals. Tables cover selected categories, not every award organization.
field_notes.country: ISO country codes from the source catalog; a network location does not verify production origin.
field_notes.language: ISO language code, checked against provider language where possible.
field_notes.tags: Controlled editorial labels. Humor/tone are unweighted lists in this release; optional original estimates are separate.
field_notes.editorial_tag_weights: Order-derived source estimates; do not use by default.
field_notes.calendar_span_years_inclusive: End year, or snapshot year for running/uncertain records, minus start plus one. Null for an unknown closed span. Includes hiatuses; not years of continuous broadcasting.
field_notes.creators_stars: References to people; imported credits remain unverified unless separately sourced.
field_notes.labels_content_audience: Editorial interpretations, not official age certificates or measured reception.
field_notes.id_aliases: Map any former show ID to the current canonical ID before joining personal ratings.
field_notes.reception_snapshots: Dated source observations with scale, denominator when known, and verification status; percentages are not interchangeable with star averages.

meta.personal_data: No user ratings, viewing history, survey answers, or inferred personal preferences are included. Those belong in a separate profile export.
meta.source_reuse: Source terms differ. TVmaze-derived fields require attribution and ShareAlike compliance. Wikipedia reference tables have their own terms; IMDb-derived input is not presented as unrestricted open data. No blanket license is asserted for all imported material.
known_limits: Source-linked does not mean every fact was independently verified.
Editorial tags, creators, production countries, networks, and most reported revival histories still require review.
Recognition evidence is incomplete and dated; candidate status is explicit.
No statement of exhaustive coverage of award winners or all sitcoms is made.
Current statuses are snapshots and can change.

changes: Reconciled all 304 distinct records and preserved both input ID namespaces.
Added per-record source links and field provenance; independently retrieved provider identity/date/season observations.
Cross-checked selected award categories and separated unverified imported claims.
Replaced misleading years_on_air with an explicitly labeled calendar span.
Separated editorial weights from primary tags and kept legacy annotations out of automatic scoring.
Restored four missing titles and explicitly classified three pre-1970 exceptions.
Removed empty personal viewing records from the shared catalog.

format.multi-cam: Multi-camera production; camera arrangement alone does not establish live versus added audience laughter.
format.single-cam: Single-camera production; this classification alone does not establish whether audience laughter is used.
format.single-cam-laugh-track: Single-camera production with reported added audience laughter; editorial, not a production audit.
format.sketch-variety: Sketches and musical bits rather than one continuing story
format.not-applicable: Camera-style category not applicable to an animated series; medium is recorded separately.

devices.fourth-wall: Characters talk directly to the viewer
devices.meta: Jokes about being a TV show or about TV itself
devices.musical-numbers: Songs or performances built into episodes
devices.live-episodes: Some episodes performed and broadcast live
devices.multi-role-star: The lead plays several different characters
devices.stylized-visuals: Unusual camera work, graphics or visual gags
devices.show-within-show: Follows the making of a fictional TV program
devices.mockumentary: Shot like a documentary, with talking-head interviews
devices.talking-animals: Animal characters who talk and act like people

humor.insult: Put-downs and roasting as a main engine
humor.absurdist: Illogical or ridiculous situations played straight
humor.satire: Targets institutions, politics, media or society
humor.parody: Spoofs a genre or other media
humor.dark: Finds comedy in bleak or taboo subjects
humor.gentle: Soft or low-stakes humor; does not establish age suitability.
humor.topical: References to current events of its day
humor.schemes: Get-rich-quick plans and plots that backfire

tone.warm: Characters basically like each other; affectionate
tone.wholesome: Earnest or values-oriented tone; does not establish age suitability.
tone.very-special-episodes: Periodic serious issue episodes with a lesson
tone.heartfelt: Emotional stakes alongside the humor; an editorial interpretation.
tone.cynical: Selfish or jaded characters; little sentiment
tone.mean-spirited: Characters are cruel to each other as the main joke
tone.socially-conscious: Engages with race, class, gender, politics or war
tone.nostalgic: Looks back fondly at an earlier era

setting.home: Family home is the main set
setting.workplace: Job site is a main set
setting.media: TV, radio, magazine, newspaper or publishing
setting.big-city: Large-city setting, with separate city-specific tags where recorded.
setting.suburbs: Suburban setting; not a country-of-production claim.
setting.small-town: Small-town setting, distinguished from a suburb or large city.
setting.period-historical: Set in an earlier century or a historical era
setting.small-city: A smaller city rather than a large metropolitan center or a rural town.

themes.parenting: Raising kids from the parents' view
themes.nanny-housekeeper: Live-in help as a lead character
themes.fish-out-of-water: Someone thrown into an unfamiliar world
themes.career-woman: A woman's professional ambitions at the center
themes.race-culture: Race and cultural identity explored directly
themes.addiction-recovery: Recovery from alcohol or drug addiction
themes.mental-illness: Mental illness as part of the premise
themes.creature: Robot, monster or creature as a main character
themes.genre-spoof: Parodies a cop, spy or soap genre
themes.mystery: A mystery to solve drives the story
themes.teacher-mentor: Teacher or mentor guiding young people
themes.nostalgia: Built on looking back at the past
themes.comedian-vehicle: Built around a stand-up comic's persona
themes.bereavement: Grief, loss, or bereavement is a recurring theme.
themes.community: Community belonging or mutual support is a recurring theme.

structure.episodic: Self-contained episodes; watch in any order
structure.mixed: Mostly standalone with ongoing relationship arcs

content.clean: Editorial impression of relatively little explicit material; not an official rating or a comprehensive viewing advisory.
content.mild: Editorial impression of occasional mild language or themes; not an official classification.
content.mature: Cable-level language, sex or dark content

cast.black-led: Black lead or predominantly Black cast
